title: Inside Proud Tek Production — Who Does What, Step by Step
summary: How a Proud Tek order is made. We own the product and antenna specification, chip sourcing, first-article approval, quality control and export packing; tooling, lamination, printing and encoding run on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our process specification. This page sets out that responsibility split, the material supply chain, the QC gates and the PO-to-dispatch workflow, so your team can evaluate production fit — and audit it — without taking a logo on trust.
heroPoints: In-house specification and quality control; tooling and production executed on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to Proud Tek's specification — the same model, in the same words, as our sister brand RFIDAK.
Every batch is 100% inspected — chip read/write, print, dimensions, packaging — and signed off by Proud Tek QC before release; production travelers and test records are retained seven years.

Production-line visits and live video walkthroughs are arranged by appointment; ask for the partner line's own certificates during quotation — our ISO certificates cover the sales and supplier-management operation.

ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 cover the sales and supplier-management operation; production runs on contracted partner lines.

sections.title: Capacity and responsibility

items.label: Encoded units functional-tested by our QC

sections.intro: Capacity is quoted per programme once chip allocation is confirmed — RFID throughput depends on the encoding scheme and the chip family in play, not on raw machine speed. We do not own the production floor: we hold reserved capacity on partner lines and commit only what the chip allocation and the line schedule support.

sections.title: On the partner line — equipment and controls
sections.intro: The main About page lists what we specify; this is where it is physically made. Lines are run by partner-line operators to Proud Tek's process specification: we approve the first article, hold the encoding and artwork masters, and our QC signs off every batch — so the pilot lot and the production order run to the same locked spec.

callout.label: What this page is, and what it is not
callout.text: The equipment and process descriptions on this page describe contracted partner lines, not premises we own, and they are our own statements. They are not covered by our ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 certificates, whose certified scope is the sales service of smart cards and RFID tags — see [/about/certifications/](/about/certifications/). Treat the descriptions as claims to be tested: book a line visit or a live video walk-through, and ask for the partner line's own certification and audit documents by name.

features.title: Partner-line equipment
features.text: Laminating, encoding, printing and die-cutting equipment on contracted lines in Shenzhen, from chip bonders to reel-to-reel programmers. Tooling and production are executed to Proud Tek's process specification; Proud Tek approves the first article and its QC signs off every batch before release.

features.title: ESD-controlled assembly
features.text: Wet-inlay bonding runs at ESD-controlled stations with wrist-strap and ionised-air discipline — bare chips and thin-film antennas are static-sensitive. Conductive-adhesive cure temperature and dwell time are logged per lot on the traveler we issue.

features.title: Anti-metal & specialty work
features.text: Ferrite-backed on-metal tags for IT-asset, tool and equipment programmes are run on a partner line with dedicated backing capability. Read range against steel and aluminium is validated per SKU and filed with the production traveler.

features.title: Reel-to-reel encoding
features.text: High-volume UHF inlay programmes run on reel-to-reel encoders with inline read-test, so multi-million-unit orders are programmed and verified in one pass rather than hand-fed unit by unit.

features.title: Engineering and QC verification
features.text: Every incoming chip batch is read-tested at the reel before it enters production; every finished batch gets chip read/write, print, dimension and packaging inspection by Proud Tek QC. Read-range and reader-compatibility checks run in our Shenzhen lab; duty-cycle tests (wash cycles, environmental, mechanical) are arranged per programme on the partner line or at accredited third-party labs.

features.title: Packaging and export
features.text: Finished goods are inspected, packed and exported by Proud Tek — FOB Shenzhen by default, DDP on request. Distributor safety-stock and scheduled call-off programmes are set up per agreement.

sections.title: Materials and supply chain
sections.intro: We treat material sourcing as a quality lever, not a cost lever. The inlay roll-stock, PVC sheet, conductive adhesive and ferrite backing are all qualified vendors with parallel sources for risk mitigation.
bullets: Inlay substrates — PET / PI roll-stock qualified from two parallel vendors; cut-sheet inlays inspected for thickness and dimensional stability before line entry.
Card stock — PVC, ABS, PETG, recycled-PVC; FSC-certified paper and bamboo composite stocks available on request (chain-of-custody documents supplied per order).
Conductive adhesive — silver-loaded epoxy from named vendors; cure cycle validated per chip family.
Ferrite backing — automotive-grade ferrite sheet for on-metal SKUs; tested against representative steel and aluminium substrates.

Chip sourcing — Proud Tek buys through authorised distribution channels for NXP, Impinj and EM Microelectronic and holds a forward stock buffer on critical SKUs; other families via authorised distribution on request.

sections.title: QC gates and verification testing
sections.intro: A 100% functional read test catches encoding faults, but a tag also has to survive its real duty cycle. The read/write, dimensional and packaging gates below are Proud Tek QC's own sign-off on every batch; the duty-cycle tests are arranged per programme — on the partner line or at an accredited third-party laboratory — before a pilot is signed off.

rows: Every chip batch read-tested at the reel before entering production — counterfeit or grey-market substitution caught at inspection
100% functional read on every encoded unit; decode-rate and UID / NDEF / EPC verification
Partner line, verified and signed off by Proud Tek QC
Print quality, dimensions, packaging and labelling against the traveler
Read distance, orientation sensitivity and reader / lock compatibility against representative surfaces
Industrial wash cycles for laundry tags, temperature / humidity exposure, adhesion and peel, bend / flex / torsion
Per programme: partner line or accredited third-party lab, report shared with the sample data

callout.label: Ask for the test data
callout.text: For a qualified programme we share the read-range plots, wash-cycle survival counts and AQL inspection results for your shortlisted SKUs as part of the sample data — useful when your own QA needs evidence before a production commitment.

sections.title: From PO to dispatch — production workflow
sections.intro: Once a production order is released, the programme runs to a documented traveler that Proud Tek issues to the partner line. Every step generates a record retained in our quality archive for at least seven years per ISO 9001 requirement.

items.label: Day 0 — PO received, traveler issued
items.text: Production traveler issued with chip allocation, encoding scheme, artwork files and packaging spec locked. Material kit pulled from stockroom; raw-material lot numbers attached to the traveler for full traceability.

items.label: Days 1-5 — Assembly and lamination
items.text: Wet-inlay assembly or card lamination runs on the partner line to the traveler. First-piece approval by Proud Tek at line start, then in-process AQL sampling. Reject rate logged; out-of-spec lots quarantined before the next step.

items.label: Days 6-10 — Encoding and marking
items.text: Encoding station runs the locked scheme to Proud Tek's encoding specification. Every encoded unit gets a functional read test; failed units rejected at the line. Laser engraving, hot stamping or print runs against the approved artwork.

items.label: Days 11-14 — Final QC, packaging, dispatch
items.text: Proud Tek QC runs the AQL final inspection on visual and dimensional attributes and signs off the batch. Packaging per spec; box-level barcode / RFID outer-pack labelling if requested. Shipment released FOB Shenzhen after the document pack (CO, COC, packing list, test reports) is signed off.

sections.title: Customer audits and production visits
sections.intro: We welcome buyer audits — they reduce procurement risk on both sides. Visits take place on the partner line producing your order and are arranged by Proud Tek; non-standard audit scope (third-party social compliance, environmental, IT security) is scoped per programme.
bullets: Buyer engineering audits — access to the wet-inlay, lamination, encoding and QC stations on the partner line producing your order, by appointment.
Quality system audits — Proud Tek's ISO 9001:2015 document review, training records, calibration logs and corrective-action archives (sales and supplier-management scope).
Third-party audits — TÜV, SGS, Intertek, Bureau Veritas and BSCI / Sedex visits accommodated when the programme requires them; the partner line's own certificates are supplied on request.
Pre-shipment inspection — your QC agent can attend Proud Tek's final AQL inspection at no additional charge.
Live video walkthrough — production lines, QC stations and warehousing shown in real time on WhatsApp for buyers who cannot travel; we schedule against your time zone.

callout.label: Audit accommodation
callout.text: If your organization has a specific audit framework (Sedex, BSCI, Higg Index, RBA, FSC chain-of-custody, etc.) mention it on the initial inquiry. We can route the certification path and absorb the audit cost as part of an annual-volume agreement when justified.

sections.title: Compliance documentation shipped with every order
sections.intro: Every shipment leaves Shenzhen with the documentation buyers actually need at customs and at brand-owner intake. Certified third-party test reports can be commissioned on a per-program basis.
bullets: Commercial invoice and packing list with chip family, SKU code and encoding lot per line item.
Certificate of Origin (Form A / GSP / FORM E / Form F) per destination market.

CE marking is a manufacturer declaration supported by test reports — our published EN 62311 RF-exposure report (BCTC2509165308-1E) covers an RFID card; reader devices are approved per device per market.
Material compliance — sample-based RoHS (XKS2025R01150076) and REACH SVHC (XKS2025R10150032E) test reports on the articles they name; testing on your exact specification can be commissioned.
Functional test report — sample lot of encoded units with read-range and decode-rate data.
ISO 9001:2015 / 14001:2015 / 45001:2018 certificate copies with numbers, scope and registrar lookup on the certifications page.

faq.question: Can you test tags against our specific duty cycle before we commit?
faq.answer: Yes. For a qualified programme we arrange the duty-cycle tests your application needs — industrial wash cycles for laundry tags, temperature and humidity exposure, adhesion and peel, bend and flex — on the partner line or at an accredited third-party laboratory, alongside read-range and reader-compatibility checks in our Shenzhen lab. The read-range plots and survival data are shared with the sample data before you place a production order. (For minimum order quantities, see the FAQ on the main About page.)

faq.question: Can you handle multi-million-unit annual programs?
faq.answer: Yes, within the capacity we hold on partner lines. Multi-million-unit UHF inlay and HF card programmes run on reel-to-reel encoding lines; capacity is quoted per programme once chip allocation is confirmed, and we do not promise capacity that depends on a chip family we cannot lock in.

faq.question: How do you handle chip allocation when global supply is constrained?
faq.answer: We buy through authorised distribution channels for NXP, Impinj and EM Microelectronic and hold a forward stock buffer on critical SKUs, with authorised-distribution backup for spot demand. When a chip family is tight we flag it before quotation and offer chip-substitution paths where the deployment context allows — never a mid-project surprise.

faq.question: Are buyer visits to the production lines welcome?
faq.answer: Yes. Visits take place on the partner line producing your order and are arranged by Proud Tek by appointment; your QC agent can attend our pre-shipment inspection at no charge. For buyers who cannot travel we run live video walkthroughs on WhatsApp — production lines, QC stations and warehousing in real time.

faq.question: What is included in the compliance documentation pack?
faq.answer: Every shipment ships with: commercial invoice, packing list, Certificate of Origin per destination market, the sample-based RoHS and REACH SVHC test reports and the EN 62311 RF-exposure report published on our certifications page (CE remains a manufacturer declaration), and a functional test report on the encoded lot. Testing on your exact specification, or third-party reports (TÜV, SGS, Intertek), can be commissioned per programme.

faq.question: How long are quality records kept?
faq.answer: Production travelers, encoding logs, QC records and material certificates are retained by Proud Tek for at least seven years per ISO 9001:2015 documented-information requirements. Records can be pulled by SKU code or encoding lot if a buyer needs traceability for a field issue or audit.
